summary: New Zealand lets visa-waiver nationals (the US, UK, EU, Canada, Japan and around 30 others) visit for up to 3 months — 6 for British citizens — but they must first obtain an NZeTA and pay the NZD 100 International Visitor Levy. Australians enter freely, everyone else needs a Visitor Visa, and every traveler must complete the digital New Zealand Traveller Declaration before arrival.

items.name: Passport
items.details: The passport you will travel on, valid for at least 3 months after the date you intend to leave New Zealand.

items.name: Photo
items.details: One acceptable photo, or a device that can take one.

fee.notes: Immigration New Zealand gives the cost as from NZD 441. It says 80% of applications are processed within 2 weeks; processing is busiest between September and March.

items.name: Copy of passport or certificate of identity
items.details: Valid for at least 3 months after the date you plan to leave New Zealand.

items.name: Chest X-ray or medical examination evidence
items.details: If required; less than 3 months old when Immigration New Zealand receives it.

items.name: Proof of funds
items.details: Proof you have enough money to live on.

items.name: Proof of your plans
items.details: Proof of your plans in New Zealand, to show you are a genuine visitor.

items.name: Proof of onward travel
items.details: Proof you can leave New Zealand at the end of your stay.

items.name: Partner and children's documents

source.name: Immigration New Zealand — Visitor Visa: documents you need

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your intended departure date from New Zealand.

travelInsurance.text: Not an entry requirement for tourists. Immigration New Zealand says visitors will need to pay for any health care or medical assistance they need, and recommends full medical insurance for the stay.

onwardTicket.text: At check-in for a flight to New Zealand, NZeTA travellers must show a paid ticket out of New Zealand to a country they have the right to enter (or a cruise itinerary or craft owner's letter if leaving by sea).

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors must be able to show NZD 1,000 per person per month of stay (NZD 400 per month if accommodation is already paid for).

declarations.name: New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD)
declarations.submitWindow: Before departure for New Zealand (opens 24 hours before flights)
declarations.text: Every traveler must complete the free digital New Zealand Traveller Declaration (website or app) before arrival, covering customs and biosecurity questions. It is linked to your passport and checked at passport control; you do not need to print anything.

source.name: New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD) — About the NZTD (New Zealand Customs Service)

currencyLimits.text: Cash of NZD 10,000 or more (or foreign equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

source.name: New Zealand Customs Service — Border Cash Report

notes: The UK says it is illegal to import most food products into New Zealand and that you must declare anything that may be prohibited; breaking the rules can mean a fine of up to NZ$100,000 or a prison sentence.

Wood and leather products, golf clubs, tents and fishing equipment can carry pests or diseases, the UK says: if in doubt, declare them to a Biosecurity New Zealand official or put them in the marked bins at the airport.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says crime levels are generally low, but street crime happens in major towns and cities and thieves may target unattended vehicles, especially hire cars and camper vans in tourist areas. It says New Zealand is in a major earthquake zone, that tsunamis can happen along the coastlines, and that weather can quickly become dangerous in some coastal and exposed areas.

tips.text: Declare any food or outdoor gear that may be prohibited, and if in doubt, declare it. The UK says it is illegal to import most food products, that tents, fishing equipment and golf clubs can carry pests, and that breaking the rules can mean a fine of up to NZ$100,000 or a prison sentence.
Complete the free New Zealand Traveller Declaration online or in the NZTD app before you fly. New Zealand Customs says everyone travelling into New Zealand must complete one, and that it is free.

Canada says traffic drives on the left. The UK notes that highways can be narrow, winding and hilly, and Canada warns that rural railway crossings may have no barriers and that dairy herds often cross main roads at milking time.
Budget for the NZD 100 International Visitor Levy on top of the NZD 17 NZeTA fee. It is charged in the same transaction and funds conservation and tourism infrastructure.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for New Zealand?
faq.answer: No visa, but they must request an NZeTA before boarding and pay the International Visitor Levy — about NZD 117 in total. Once granted, it is valid for 2 years and allows visits of up to 3 months.

faq.question: How much does the NZeTA really cost?
faq.answer: The NZeTA request fee is NZD 17, but almost all tourists also pay the NZD 100 International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) in the same transaction, so expect about NZD 117. Immigration New Zealand says to use the official NZeTA website or app.

faq.question: Do Australians need an NZeTA or visa for New Zealand?
faq.answer: No. Immigration New Zealand says Australian citizens need neither a visa nor an NZeTA. Australian permanent residents (non-citizens), however, do need an NZeTA.

faq.question: What is the New Zealand Traveller Declaration?
faq.answer: The NZTD is a free digital declaration every traveler must complete before arriving, at travellerdeclaration.govt.nz or in the NZTD app. It covers customs and biosecurity questions and replaces the old paper arrival card.

faq.question: How long can I stay in New Zealand as a visitor?
faq.answer: Visa-waiver visitors get up to 3 months per visit (6 months for British citizens), with a maximum of 6 months in any 12-month period. For longer stays, apply for a Visitor Visa, which can allow up to 9 months.
